Kuvitus: koulun laboratorion työpöytä. P: Illustration: a work bench in a school laboratory. On the bench there is a breadboard where a battery holder and a lamp holder are connected with wires in the same circuit, and the lamp is lit. Next to it is a grey digital multimeter whose red and black test leads touch the two terminals of the lamp holder.
Kaksi kytkentäkaaviota. Vasemmalla paris: Two circuit diagrams. On the left the battery, the lamp and the ammeter A are in the same loop one after another: the ammeter is in series with the lamp, and the same current I passes through the battery, the meter and the lamp. On the right the battery and the lamp form a loop, and the voltmeter V is connected between the terminals of the lamp, in parallel with the lamp. The purple arrows show the direction of the current from the positive terminal of the battery to the negative terminal.
Drawing of a digital multimeter. At the top the display with the reading 1.500 V. In the middle the selector, around which are the measuring ranges 2 V, 20 V, 200 mA and 10 A; the pointer is on the range 2 V. At the bottom three jacks: COM, V mA and 10 A. The place of the black lead is COM and that of the red lead V mA or 10 A. On the right the labels display, selector and jacks.
Kaksi väärää kytkentää. Vasemmalla virta: Two wrong connections. On the left the ammeter A is connected in parallel with the lamp. The current passes almost entirely through the ammeter of small resistance, which is shown by the thick purple arrow: the lamp is not lit, and the current is large. On the right the voltmeter V is in series with the lamp. The large resistance of the meter decreases the current to almost zero, so the lamp is not lit and there are no current arrows.
Kuva mittakaavassa: jännitteen akseli vä: Picture to scale: the voltage axis from 1.46 V to 1.54 V. The upper segment shows the reading 1.50 V obtained on the range 20 V and its error limit ±0.03 V, that is the interval 1.47 V–1.53 V. The lower segment shows the reading 1.500 V obtained on the range 2 V and its error limit ±0.010 V, that is the interval 1.490 V–1.510 V. The segment of the lower range is about a third of the length of the upper one.
